subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Sanctions and Watchlists
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Sanctions and Watchlists.

hook.text: OFAC maintains lists of sanctioned people and entities. Doing business with anyone on the list is a federal crime.

buildup.text: Banks must screen every transaction against sanctions lists from OFAC, the UN, the EU, and others.

discovery.text: BNP Paribas paid $8.9 billion — the largest sanctions fine ever — for processing payments for Sudan, Iran, and Cuba.

twist.text: Name matching is imperfect. Millions of false positives clog compliance teams while real hits can be missed.

climax.text: Sanctions screening is mandatory, expensive, and error-prone. But skipping it invites devastating penalties.

punchline.text: $8.9 billion fine. Screen every transaction. Or else.

quiz.question: What was BNP Paribas fined $8.9 billion for?
